layout_details.content: # Annex B
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: # Legacy coding and coding from the traditional publication chains (including possible differences between IEC and ISO)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## B.1 Reasons for coding differences
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Historically, the two organisations each applied their own tagging to their XML documents. With the arrival of NISO STS v.1.0, discussions were taken up to harmonise the XML, the first result being edition 1.0 of the present Coding guidelines.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The use of OSD has now made it necessary to fully align on the XML content. Metadata still contain differences.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Differences in tagging, which were originally described in the main body of this document, have now been moved to the annex as they only apply to legacy content, respectively content coming out of the traditional publication chain.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Where contents or usages are different between ISO and IEC,the ISO variant is provided in a red box,the IEC variant in a blue one.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
ISO variant ...
IEC variant ...
layout_details.label: table

layout_details.content: ## B.2 Traditional and legacy coding
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## B.2.1 Front matter
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The following front and back matter content are not captured in the XML:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - cover pages
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - table of contents
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - page headers and footers containing the name of the document, page numbers etc.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - index if it refers to page numbers (if coded, indexes refer to marked-up elements, and only in XML from the traditional publication chain - OSD does not generate indexes)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The copyright notices listed in the footer in the PDF document are captured in the metadata section using <permissions>.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In addition to the elements listed in 4.2, the front matter of a standard may contain prose material, such as notes and sections, particularly as used for placeholder elements not articulated in NISO
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: STS (for example, patents or particular copyright statements) or for older content with different structures.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## B.2.2 Use of <sec> for custom subdivisions
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Legacy documents sometimes have non-standard subdivisions, such as chapters or other groupings of content. For these, <sec> is used.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## B.2.3 @content-type for indexes
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: @content-type in <back> can also be index
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## B.2.4 Lists of references (normative / bibliographic) with designators
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A reference in the normative reference section that is not a standard is coded as it appears (including punctuation and label) using <mixed-citation>.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Case 1:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - W3C XML 1.0:2000, Extensible Markup Language (XML) 1.0 (Second Edition), W3C Recommendation, Copyright $ \circ $ [6 October 2000] World Wide Web Consortium, (Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Institut National de Recherche en Informatique et en Automatique, Keio University), http://www.w3.org/TR/2000/REC-xml-20001006.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: is coded as:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```xml

<ref>

    <label>—</label>

    <mixed-citation>W3C XML 1.0:2000, Extensible Markup Language (XML) 1.0

(Second Edition), W3C Recommendation. Copyright  [6 October 2000] World Wide Web

Consortium, (Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Institut National de Recherche en

Informatique et en Automatique, Keio University), <uri

xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">http://www.w3.org/TR/2000/REC-xml-

20001006</uri>.</mixed-citation>

</ref>

```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Case 2:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
- W3C XML Schema:2001, XML Schema Part 2: Datatypes, W3C Recommendation, Copyright $ \textcircled{c} $ [2 May 2001] World Wide Web Consortium, (Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Institut National de Recherche en Informatique et en Automatique, Keio University), http://www.w3.org/TR/2001/REC-xmlschema-2-20010502.

NOTE - When the reference "W3C XML Schema" is used in this Recommendation | International Standard, it refers to W3C XML Schema Part 1 and W3C XML Schema Part 2.

- IETF RFC 2396 (1998), Uniform Resource Identifiers (URI): Generic Syntax.

- IETF RFC 1766 (1995), Tags for the Identification of Languages.

(Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Institut National de Recherche en Informatique et en Automatique, Keio University), http://www.w3.org/TR/2001/REC-xmlschema-2- 20010502.

When the reference "W3C XML Schema" is used in this Recommendation | International Standard, it refers to W3C XML Schema Part 1 and W3C XML Schema Part 2.

 IETF RFC 2396 (1998), Uniform Resource Identifiers (URI): Generic Syntax. ```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: If a reference has a recognizable designator such as [1] (more commonly used in the bibliography section) then this is coded as a <label> within the <ref>.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In <mixed-citation>, any presentation formatting is captured as such, e.g. <bold>, <italic>.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## B.2.5 Numbered paragraphs
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Legacy content may not have the attribute @sec-type="numbered-paragraph".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## B.2.6 Back matter
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Indexes and footnotes
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In addition to the elements mentioned in 4.5, the back matter can contain indexes and / or, in IEC legacy documents, footnotes (as described below).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Annex type coding
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A difference between IEC and ISO persists in the explicit coding of <annex-type> in the traditional publication chains:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## ISO
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The ISO coding duplicates information between @content-type and <annex-type>, but allows flexibility when rendering or extracting data. This will be done in content produced from eXtyles.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```html

<app-group>

    <app content-type="informative" id="sec_A">

    <label>Annex A</label><annex-type>(informative)</annex-type><title>Types of

proficiency testing schemes</title>

```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## IEC
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The annex type is not coded as text but will be derived from @content-type on rendering. IEC legacy files may have different @content-type values: inform / norm.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## B.2.7 Spaces, punctuation and formatting
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Especially in legacy publications, there are elements such as spaces, tabs and line breaks, that serve formatting purposes. These should be replaced wherever possible or deleted if they are not necessary during the conversion to XML, unless they are significant, such as in formulae, tables, and example code.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Sequential spacing characters should be coded as a single space, unless they are significant.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Where spacing characters or tabs have been used to align blocks of text into columns, the text should instead be coded in a table or array.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## IEC legacy tagging
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In IEC legacy publications, spaces are maintained in form fields.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Non-breaking spaces can be inserted to prevent automatic line breaks between two text portions. The following are a few patterns where a non-breaking space (  or  ) should be used.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: These are usually found when the text follows/precedes numbers or numbering text such as A,B,C... or a,b,c ...
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Some examples:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: [number] [SI Unit]
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: (Part)[space] ([0-9])
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: (ISO)[space]([0-9])
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: (ISO/TC)[space]([0-9])
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
$$
(\mathrm {N o t e}) [ \mathrm {s p a c e} ] ([ 0 - 9 ] [ \mathrm {s p a c e} ] \mathrm {t o e n t r y:})
$$
layout_details.label: formula

layout_details.content:
$$
(\mathrm {T a b l e}) [ \mathrm {s p a c e} ] ([ 0 - 9 ])
$$
layout_details.label: formula

layout_details.content:
$$
(\mathrm {F o r m u l a}) [ \mathrm {s p a c e} ] ([ \backslash ((0 - 9) ^ {*} \backslash) ])
$$
layout_details.label: formula

layout_details.content: (Figure) [space] ([0-9])
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: (Clause)[space]([0-9])
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
$$
(\mathrm {V o l u m e}) [ \mathrm {s p a c e} ] ([ 0 - 9 ])
$$
layout_details.label: formula

layout_details.content:
$$
(\mathrm {A t i c l e}) [ \mathrm {s p a c e} ] ([ \mathrm {A} - \mathrm {Z} | \mathrm {a} - \mathrm {z} ] [ | \backslash . | \backslash) ])
$$
layout_details.label: formula

layout_details.content: (Step)[space]（[0-9]）
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
$$
(\mathrm {O I M L}) [ \mathrm {s p a c e} ] (\mathrm {D})
$$
layout_details.label: formula

layout_details.content:
$$
(\mathrm {A n n e x}) [ \mathrm {s p a c e} ] ([ \mathrm {A} - Z | a - z ] [ | \cdot | \cdot ])
$$
layout_details.label: formula

layout_details.content: [space]（—[A-Z]）
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: [0-9] [space] [mathematical sign] [space] [0-9] (for formulae and other dyadic expressions) certain expressions do not require space: [mathematical sign] [0-9] [unit], e.g. $ + 3^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Numbers formatted with spaces, e.g. 1 000: a non-breaking space should be used, e.g. 1 000.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: When processing legacy documents, it is recommended that non-standard fonts used for a semantic reason should be preserved. All punctuation characters (except soft hyphens) are to be considered significant and preserved.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Superscript, subscript, italic, bold, underlined, small caps, strike-through, mono-spaced etc. text is coded as it appears using: <sup>, <sub>, <italic>, <bold>, <underlined>, <sc>, <strike>, <monospace> etc.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The element <sc> is used to mark text that should appear in a font that creates smaller capital letters ("small caps"). Uppercase letters included in the tags will be preserved.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.label: text

In legacy content, sometimes alignment has been defined in an attribute of

Possible values of @style-type in

layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## B.2.9 Formatting text with <styled-content>
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In legacy content and redline documents, when text styling is used to convey meaning, this shall be done using <styled-content> rather than direct formatting ( <bold>, <italic> etc.).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attributes
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: @style-type
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: @style
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## @style-type / @specific-use
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: These attributes are most often used to mark up additions and deletions in redline documents.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ISO
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Values for @style-type (in addition to those for alignment mentioned in ):
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - addition (for additions, e.g. in redline versions; rendering will be in green)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - deletion (for deletions, e.g. in redline versions; rendering will be in red and strikethrough)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: IEC
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Values for @specific-use:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - insert (for additions, e.g. in redline versions; rendering will be in green)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - delete (for deletions, e.g. in redline versions; rendering will be in red and strikethrough)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.label: text

layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Unnumbered formulae can appear inline, but also as block formulae.

layout_details.content: ## Subfigures and multiple graphics within a figure
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## ISO
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The caption of a sub-figure (e.g. "a) - title of sub-figure") is coded in <title> within a <caption> within the <graphic>.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The rest of the sub-figure caption should be captured as a label within the <graphic> (excluding any trailing dash), for example:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```html

<graphic xlink:href="fig_1.1" id="fig_1.1">

    <label>a)</label>

    <caption><title>title of sub-figure</title></caption>

</graphic>

```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## IEC
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: If the figure contains multiple graphics, then each graphic is captured as a separate <graphic> within <fig>.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: If the figure consists of multiple sub-figures (each with their own caption), then each subfigure is captured as a separate <fig> inside <figure-group>.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Each sub-figure has an @id based on its label.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```html

<fig-group id="fig-3">

3 m separation distance, Table-top EUT</title></caption>

<fig id="fig-3a">

<label>Figure 3a</label>

<caption>

<title>Top view</title></caption>
```

layout_details.content: ## Usage of TBX vs. <term-display>
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: There are two different options for tagging terms and definitions. Both structures occur optionally inside the <term-sec> container element:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - one is TBX
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - the other is a simpler, less powerful alternative, <term-display>.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
ISO ISO uses TBX exclusively.
IEC IEC uses TBX wherever possible. In redline documents and certain series where the elements are arranged in a special way and layout is important to the entry, IEC also uses
layout_details.label: table

layout_details.content: The <term-sec> container element also includes <label>, which contains the number of the terminological entry.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## TBX (based exclusively on semantic information)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: TBX is a concept-oriented exchange format for data from terminological databases. The TBX element <tbx:termEntry> models a term using the TBX-namespace vocabulary and ontology for terms. It can record information about any number of synonymous terms and multiple languages. The TBX vocabulary in NISO STS is derived and extended from ISO 30042. For usage information and contents, see the documentation at:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: https://www.iso.org/schema/nisosts/v0.2/doc/tbx/index.html
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Part of speech
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In NISO STS v.1.0, there was no value "undefined". Therefore, all legacy conversion used "noun" as the default value. While this may be correct in most cases, it is not a reliable value. We therefore recommend not basing any programming on this value.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## <term-display> (more appearance oriented)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The NISO STS element <term-display> uses natural language to describe terms, and may incorporate semantic term elements such as definition (<def>) and part of speech (<part-of speech>). Semantic tagging is encouraged, but not enforced. It is a more appearance-oriented encoding of terminological data that may be used when:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - it is difficult to generate the desired formatted display from a TBX entry
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - converting back-catalogue documents, in cases where it is difficult to create a useful TBX term entry from an appearance-oriented input document
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Generally, ISO and IEC will use TBX. In some cases of legacy conversion, however, IEC uses <termdisplay> to ensure all elements are correctly displayed. For usage, see below.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## IDs
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The ID of the terminological entry is derived from the entry number contained in <label> and is used for both <term-sec> and <tbx:termEntry>. IEC has an @id on <tbx:term> as well.

</term-sec>

<tbx:term-entry>: @id has prefix “te-”

<tbx:term>: @id corresponds to the term itself
